background.description: Legacy pilot approximation only: --mix population retains these four request weights and one-property writes. Main --mix journeys uses execution_v2.

demand_formula: N / 86400 * (active_fraction * sum(actions * logical_reads * (1-cache_hit) * pod_fanout / batch_factor) + background_reads + active_fraction * content_writes + policy_changes) * offered_multiplier

arrival_schedule.method: Poisson scheduled arrivals; schedule generated before run; same schedule replayed in paired languages
arrival_schedule.retry_policy: no automatic retries; every offered request retains its first scheduled timestamp
arrival_schedule.overload: count unsent, rejected, timed-out and late arrivals; never lower offered rate when responses slow
arrival_schedule.cross_pod: fanout creates separately authorized target-Pod requests; this does not measure an unbounded federation operator

latency_budget.interpretation: Declared usability targets. Measure complete journeys; component p95 values cannot be added to infer a journey p95. Network profiles are experimental conditions, not population measurements.

evidence.supports: many service domains and heterogeneity of online use
evidence.does_not_support: chosen action counts, retention, daily-active fraction or backend QPS

evidence.supports: application fanout and caching affect backend request volume
evidence.does_not_support: transferring Facebook rates or cache-hit fractions to Solid

evidence.supports: measure user-relevant latency and availability objectives explicitly

activity_anchor.source_locator: Results / Objective Data; Methods / Participants and Procedure
activity_anchor.recruitment: University of Lincoln staff and students, Android owners, recruited age range 18 to 33
activity_anchor.measured_unit: device entering an interactive state; includes some calls/music, not necessarily screen-on or an application/backend request
activity_anchor.model_connection: The chosen 72 journeys per active person per day is an order-of-magnitude scenario near this observed interaction count; the activity sensitivity spans 18 to 288 journeys. No one-to-one conversion is assumed.
activity_anchor.limitations: Small selected historical cohort; device interactions can trigger zero or many journeys and backend requests; does not estimate contemporary population traffic or a statistical confidence bound on Solid demand.

calibration_status: Numeric journey, caching, activity, network and background parameters are declared scenario assumptions. The external activity anchor supplies a limited scale check, not fitted backend request rates. No empirical claim about future all-service Solid request rates is licensed by this file.

execution_v2.provenance: Prospective scenario assumptions, not measured future Solid traffic.
execution_v2.owner_read_target: First ceil(active_fraction * N) Pods; uniform or 80/20 within cohort. Corpus volume assignment is independent of Pod ID.
execution_v2.other_read_target: All hosted Pods; same selected read skew; recipient0 is the target Pod local synthetic collaborator.

background_read_template.sparql: PREFIX p: <https://sparq.dev/bench/personal#> SELECT (COUNT(?s) AS ?count) WHERE { GRAPH ?g { ?s a p:Record } }

execution_v2.retention_model: Stationary stock in expectation: daily ingestion and expiry records each equal actual retained service inventory / (history_months * 30). Ratings use this declared horizon too. Contacts are a snapshot and excluded from ingestion/expiry. Finite runs need not balance; successful receipts determine actual net stock.
execution_v2.foreground_ingestion_target: Active cohort, weighted by retained service records; adjusted to keep the same aggregate half of all-Pod volume regardless of active fraction.
execution_v2.background_mutation_target: All hosted Pods, weighted by actual retained service inventory. Read skew does not alter stock-derived write intensity.
execution_v2.expiry_target: Oldest baseline records by (creation date, record number), nonoverlapping scheduled ranges per Pod/service. Exhaustion is an offered plan failure, never wraparound.
execution_v2.modify_target: Newest half of baseline records, uniformly selected; replace p:value with 10000 + unique scheduled revision. Deleted records are no-ops, reported by actual receipt.
execution_v2.insert_identity: Unique --mutation-epoch in [0,2^20), sequence in [0,2^30); batch_id = epoch * 2^30 + sequence. Fresh independent run corpus or unique epochs required; no retries.
execution_v2.virtual_insert_date: January 2026, newest populated resource graph; this fixed-topology finite-window workload excludes resource/container creation.
execution_v2.policy_rule: Alternating scheduled desired grant/revoke of calendar recipient. Scheduling advances desired state even if dropped; count attempts, admitted requests, acknowledged changes and zero-delta no-ops separately. Administrative editing authorization is shared manifest-owner management for both languages.
execution_v2.receipt_boundary: Owner-only bounded selected-record before/after snapshots inside timed server operation; actual inserted/deleted triples, records and poststate hashes are durably journaled before acknowledgement. Client transport errors have unknown commit until journal reconciliation.
execution_v2.schedule_boundary: Marked Poisson server-request stream weighted by journey-derived demand; requests are independently scheduled, not a simulation of complete sequential UI journeys. Network journey experiments remain separate.

family_notes.activity-path: Bounded two-edge owner/inverse-owner path within a monthly activity graph; no arbitrary transitive traversal.
family_notes.social: Media browsing and communication/contact joins; no separately modeled social feed service.
family_notes.calendar-not-exists: Appointments with no readable contact name; absence may follow authorization or data state.

demand_formula_v2: sum_j(active*N*journey_requests_per_active_day) + 12*N + sum_service(total_stock/retention_days * (1/ingest_batch + 1/expire_batch + modification_ratio/modify_batch)) + contact_stock/365 + .02*N; divide by86400 and multiply scenario.
